title: Josh and Chuck Make It Through Male Puberty
summary: Josh and Chuck cover male puberty: the hormonal trigger chain (GnRH in the hypothalamus, GPR54, pituitary, LH and FSH, testosterone), the five Tanner stages with their physical changes (testicles, height, pubic hair, voice cracking, acne, body odor), the psychological and emotional side of adolescence, and cultural male coming-of-age rituals around the world. They open with a discussion of falling female menarche ages and close with a listener email about a broken pinky after a coincidence while listening.

segments.title: Opening banter and health class memories
segments.summary: The hosts joke about their own health class experiences with a PE teacher and introduce the episode on male puberty. They note the topic is worth covering for kids who aren't taught it at home.

segments.title: Declining age of puberty and menarche
segments.summary: They discuss the drop in the average age of puberty over roughly 150 years, citing the earlier average age of menarche, and evolutionary biologists' view that the older age was a relic of agricultural-era infections and poor nutrition. They also note boys may be starting puberty younger.

segments.title: Range of puberty timing and the Tanner scale
segments.summary: They explain that boys' puberty timing varies, reassure late bloomers, and introduce Richard Tanner and the one-to-five Tanner scale based on genitalia and pubic hair growth.

segments.title: Hormonal trigger: GnRH, GPR54 and the hypothalamus
segments.summary: The hosts describe how puberty begins when gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) is released from the hypothalamus, with GPR54 contact triggering it, in a process they compare to a Rube Goldberg machine.

segments.title: Stage one of puberty
segments.summary: Stage one begins around nine to ten years old with testicles and scrotum growing, height growth about two inches a year, first pubic hairs (pubarche), and first erections. They discuss why humans aren't born reproductive and mention a 1950s educational film.

segments.title: Stage two: testosterone and rapid growth
segments.summary: Around twelve or thirteen, testicles keep growing and testosterone production starts. Testosterone receptors on bone cells drive faster growth of two to three inches a year, pubic hair darkens and curls, and the body leans out.

segments.title: Stage three: voice cracking and facial changes
segments.summary: Around thirteen or fourteen the penis begins to grow, height grows about three inches a year, and the voice deepens. Vocal cords thicken and vibrate at lower frequencies, the larynx grows and forms the Adam's apple, and sinus growth in the facial bones deepens the voice further.

segments.title: Stage four: acne, body odor and hygiene
segments.summary: Around fourteen or fifteen, armpit and facial hair appear, the voice drops further, and acne begins. They explain sebum, dead skin cells and bacteria as causes, give gentle-washing advice, and joke about shower reluctance. Body odor from apocrine sweat glands is also covered.

segments.title: Stage five, height growth, and pubic hair function
segments.summary: Around fourteen to eighteen boys grow most of their height, up to about five inches a year, with broader shoulders and muscle filling out. They discuss the evolutionary purpose of pubic hair as a signal of maturity and a carrier of pheromones, and mention girls often growing earlier. Other physical changes include weight gain, larger hands and feet, clumsiness, blood pressure increase and lower metabolism.

segments.title: Precocious puberty and nocturnal emissions
segments.summary: They note early puberty before age nine can warrant a doctor visit and mention precocious puberty. They also cover nocturnal emissions (wet dreams) and normal involuntary erections.

segments.title: Hormone pathway: LH, FSH, and testicular function
segments.summary: They recap the hormonal chain: GnRH drives the pituitary to release luteinizing hormone and follicle-stimulating hormone, which act on the testes to produce testosterone (via Leydig cells) and sperm (via seminiferous tubules). Testosterone's broad effects are reviewed, with the King of the Hill character Joseph cited as an example of a pubescent boy.

segments.title: Psychological changes and adolescence
segments.summary: The hosts discuss brain development, new interests, anxiety about the future, attraction to others, reward pathway shifts, self-awareness, and pubescent depression. They advise parents to keep communication open and consider counseling. They distinguish puberty (physical) from adolescence (social and psychological).

segments.title: Male coming-of-age rituals around the world
segments.summary: They survey how cultures mark male puberty: the American punch in the arm, Islamic responsibility after first ejaculation, the Jewish bar mitzvah at thirteen, and the Sharing Out Loud Jacob the bar mitzvah boy sketch. They then describe circumcision and walkabout among Aboriginal Australians, the Sambia ritual of semen ingestion in Papua New Guinea, scarification and ant-bed trials in East Africa, the Lucenо (Lucano) ant-bed ritual, and the Matis hunting trials in Brazil.

segments.title: Listener mail: broken pinky coincidence
segments.summary: Andrew of Wooster, Ohio writes that he broke his pinky after tripping while listening to an episode on how bones break, and needed surgery with a titanium plate. He sends congratulations to his fiancee Ali Spence.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts invite listeners to share superstition stories on social media and email, and point to the website for more episodes.
